title: The water goes somewhere
hook: Twelve wet shirts dry indoors. How much water goes into the room's air?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that all the water held in a wet load ends up in the room's air as it dries, so the total is the water per item times the number of items

misconception: A load of laundry drying indoors gives off only a little water.
objective: Water leaving laundry enters the surroundings. This example multiplies retained water per item by the item count; it is a mass balance, not a forecast of room humidity.

claims.note: FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Rendered safety line (spec.warning): 'Dry indoors with a window open or a vent on: the water you dry goes into the room's air, and without ventilation it can cause damp and mould.' The physical clause is a mass balance (water that leaves the laundry enters the room air), as earlier passes found. The damp-and-mould clause now rests on opened public-health research on PMC. Int J Environ Res Public Health 2020, 'Fungal Contaminants in Energy Efficient Dwellings: Impact of Ventilation Type' (PMC7400204): indoor mould proliferation 'could be a result of water leakage or inadequate ventilation'. Air-tightening may 'promote moisture accumulation through human activities (e.g., showering, cooking, drying laundry)', and 'High moisture levels are associated with fungal growth'; mechanical ventilation lowers bedroom humidity and 'has been associated to an absence of visible moulds'. Environ Health Perspect 1986, 'Indirect health effects of relative humidity in indoor environments' (PMC1474709): 'Most species of fungi cannot grow unless the relative humidity exceeds 60%.' Cochrane 2015 (PMC6769180) lists 'exhausting water vapour from kitchens and bathrooms' among damp remediations. These are research papers, not a housing body's guidance page, but they support the line as worded ('can cause'). Builder (non-blocking): replace 'Source owed' in the source field with these citations. | FC lane-A (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, base cdee168c): VERIFIED. Rendered warning (home-lessons.ts line 1152) matches the text. Source of the kind the safety record asks for (a public-health body's guidance), opened first-hand via the PMC OAI API: AWMF mold guideline 'Medical clinical diagnostics for indoor mold exposure', Update 2023, AWMF Register No. 161/001, Allergologie Select 2024, PMC11097193 (guideline of the Association of the Scientific Medical Societies in Germany; contributors include the German Environment Agency). It says mold growth 'is therefore favored by high humidity, inadequate ventilation, and cold component surfaces', 'The living area should be kept dry by ventilation', and 'If possible, dry wet towels and other laundry outside or in a designated, well-ventilated room.' That supports 'without ventilation it can cause damp and mould' and the ventilate advice. Non-blocking, for cm-lifehacks and the safety reviewer: the guideline is stricter than the card; its prevention list also says 'Do not dry laundry in the interior.' Builder (non-blocking): replace 'Source owed' in the source field with this citation. Record: company/reviews/drying-room-water-load/2026-10-16-fact-check-lane-a.md.
